tagline: From saved videos to places you’ll actually go.
brief: Sokka turns TikTok and Instagram posts into real places on your personal map. Save and organize restaurants, cafés and travel discoveries.
promise: Turn saved places into actual plans
question: How do you make “all your saved places, on one map” feel immediately useful?
overview: The most useful references start with a familiar moment: too many saved videos, too many tabs, and no idea where to go. The map becomes the payoff, not the opening explanation.
searchNotes: Verified references from need-guided and nearby-value searches.
The examples show observable approaches, not a causal ranking of winning formats.
Metrics are indexed snapshots. The same approach can perform differently on your account.

references.title: Saved on TikTok. Lost when you need it.
references.creator: inbetweenpics
references.caption: not all TikTok viral places are worth your  money either 😅  I have authentic and genuinely amazing restaurants on my list that are worth checking out. Especially the local small businesses. 🔗 Find the guide through the link in my bio
references.transcript: Most travelers ruin their first day in Barcelona like this. They land tired, hungry, pick the first restaurant they see, and end up eating at an overpriced tourist trap. Hi, I'm Diana. I have been living in Barcelona for five years and I created something I wish I had when I first visited Barcelona. Whenever I travel, I spend hours saving restaurants from TikTok, but once I actually arrive, I never know which ones are nearby when I'm hungry. So I end up scrolling my phone for 20 minutes trying to figure out where to eat. That's why I created my Barcelona Guide. It has over 300 of my favorite restaurants, cafes, bakeries, rooftop bars, and hidden gems, all organized inside Google Maps. Imagine it's lunchtime, you're hungry, instead of searching TikTok again or walking 30 minutes across the city, you simply open Google Maps and instantly find one of my favorite restaurants just a few minutes away. Everything is already organized for you so you spend less time searching and more time actually enjoying Barcelona. Because you didn't fly all the way to Spain just to eat at a restaurant with pictures on the menu. Don't waste your vacation trying to figure out where to go. Grab my Barcelona Guide through the link in my bio, then click Barcelona Guide.

references.title: A better walk starts with saved places.
references.creator: isabellacarrr
references.transcript: I plan my psychotically long walks for tools that I use to make sure that they are the best they can possibly be. We start off with Google Maps. Pick two locations at the streets so that I know what to expect and that it's going to be an aesthetically pleasing, overall pleasing experience because you can go from point A to point B. It can be a really awesome experience or it can be a horrible experience really depending on the route that you take. VEA. I organize my walks. I'm out and about on any given day. Photos of things that I want to revisit. Save them in VEA and then I'll go back when I'm planning my walks to pinpoint the things that I have saved as places to stop or pass. Favorite feature is that you can take a photo, a live photo in the app and it saves it, geolocates it and categorizes it in the app for you. I love this because so many times when I'm on my walks, I'll take a photo of something and be like, oh my god, I have to come back to this and then it gets lost in the void of my camera roll. VEA, I take the photo, it automatically saves it and I know exactly where it is. Use it and save their locations. Inspo for where I should stop, places that are good to stop, and like bounce ideas off each other. So you can save locations from Google Maps directly into VEA. Find a taco place that I really want to stop at. I can find it on Google Maps, save it to VEA and then it's in my folder of places I want to stop. Klema. When I start my walks, I block all social media with Klema. The whole point of these walks is to connect the external world, to be in the present, to decompress and get away from things that make you anxious like social media. Forcibly blocks you out of the app. If you try to go to it, it says no, no, no. We love her. Next is Apple Podcasts, Spotify or Libby. I want to optimize these walks to be the most beneficial they possibly can. Either do silence or one of these podcasts or educational videos. Cool, you can start your walk and by the end of it, you're super educated about some random topic or discipline. So if I'm not listening to a podcast or just literally like contemplating life, I'm on the phone with my mother, my sister or my cousin. These are the tools and apps that I use to make my walks the best that they can possibly be. I hope that this was helpful and you guys will take your own psychologically long walk. Bye.

references.title: Travel posts become a real itinerary.
references.creator: david.and.rebecca
references.caption: This is a great way to make traveling easier in Korea! The App will do everything for you, from saving the things you want to do, finding their locations, create an itinerary and even let you book a K-Ride taxi!  If you are interested to try them out you can join the Trip Builder x k.ride event through the link in my bio!  1️⃣ Sign up on the event page (email + phone) 2️⃣Save 3 travel posts on Trip Builder 3️⃣ Book a k.ride to the place you saved 4️⃣Submit your proof- 2 screenshots (your 3 saved posts + your k.ride receipt) 🎁 They will review it and send your KRW 5,000 Olive Young or Starbucks mobile coupon within 24 hours! ⌛First 200 travelers only (100 Olive Young + 100 Starbucks) #TripBuilder_global #KRide_official #AITravelAssistant #Koreatravel #southkorea
references.transcript: If you're planning to come to Korea and you're looking for an easy way to travel and do fun things, then this is the video for you. Traveling in Korea can be quite stressful, especially when there's too many things to do. That's why I decided to show you a great way to travel in Korea, and it's called the Trip Builder app. All you have to do is find places on Instagram that you want to visit and save them directly onto the app, like eating Dakarvi, visiting the popular Songsoo, and even the famous library at Koek. The app will find all the locations for you, and you can even ask the AI travel assistant to create you an entire itinerary based off the places you chose. And my favorite part is that you can access the K-Ride app directly through Trip Builder and take a taxi to one of the places that you save. This is such an easy, stress-free way to travel around Korea, and I highly recommend it to those who want to travel around but don't know how to start. If you're interested to try them out, they even have an event going on where you can save three places on Trip Builder and use the K-Ride ones to receive a 5,000 won Olive Young or Starbucks gift card.

angles.title: Start with the mess.
angles.label: PROBLEM → PAYOFF
angles.description: Make viewers recognize their own saved-video problem before introducing the app.
angles.whyItFits: Sokka resolves something people already do: collecting places without making them usable.
angles.evidence: The Barcelona creator describes scrolling through saved TikToks when hungry. The Paris planner turns scattered tabs into one place.
angles.suggestedHook: You saved 47 restaurants. So… where are we eating?
angles.visualDirection: A fast stack of saved food videos, a hesitant pause, then a single clean map.

angles.title: Let the product prove it.
angles.label: VISIBLE TRANSFORMATION
angles.description: Show the few gestures that turn a video into a place. The result should be understandable without a feature list.
angles.whyItFits: Sharing a post and seeing its place appear is Sokka’s shortest explanation.
angles.evidence: Trip Builder shows saving travel posts. The reference planner and walking routine give the map a concrete role.
angles.suggestedHook: That place from your feed? It’s on your map now.
angles.visualDirection: A source video, the share action, and the saved place. Keep the original and the result together.

angles.title: Give it a real occasion.
angles.label: SITUATION FIRST
angles.description: Anchor the app in tonight’s dinner, a walk or the first day of a trip.
angles.whyItFits: A specific moment gives an abstract map a reason to matter right now.
angles.evidence: The walking routine, Barcelona’s first-day problem and Korea trip demonstration all use a recognizable occasion.
angles.suggestedHook: Your friend says “pick somewhere.” Open this.
angles.visualDirection: A message from a friend, nearby saved places, and one choice that becomes a real plan.
